alerts.title: Carbamazepine reduces DTG levels
alerts.message: Guidelines state carbamazepine decreases dolutegravir (DTG) levels by 30-70% and recommend using valproic acid as an alternative anti-epileptic. The patient is on DTG-based ART (TLD) and started carbamazepine two weeks ago. The patient now has a detectable viral load of 1,240 copies/mL despite reported good adherence. This timing suggests the new carbamazepine may be causing subtherapeutic DTG levels, leading to virologic failure.

evidence.recommended_action: Consider switching from carbamazepine to valproic acid (already on valproate) or consult neurology for an alternative that does not interact with DTG.

alerts.title: Detectable VL needs action plan
alerts.message: Guidelines recommend enhanced adherence support and repeating viral load in 2-3 months if VL is >50 copies/mL for patients on DTG-based ART. The patient's VL is 1,240 copies/mL. The clinician's plan notes the detectable VL but does not specify adherence support or a repeat VL timeline, focusing only on carbamazepine toxicity. A guideline-based management plan for the virologic breakthrough is missing.

evidence.recommended_action: Provide enhanced adherence support, address potential side-effects, and schedule a repeat viral load test in 2-3 months as per guidelines.

alerts.title: Carbamazepine toxicity and hyponatremia
alerts.message: The patient has symptoms (nystagmus, ataxia, tremor) and a supratherapeutic carbamazepine level of 14 mcg/mL (range 4-12), confirming toxicity. Hyponatremia (sodium 128 mmol/L) is also present, which is a known side effect of carbamazepine. The clinician's plan to reduce the dose and repeat the level is appropriate for managing the toxicity.

evidence.recommended_action: Continue with plan to reduce carbamazepine dose, repeat level, and monitor sodium. Consider neurology consultation.
